schema.description: One abnormal high heart rate alert the Garmin watch raised. The health ETL (ductile-healthdata fit_events.py) decodes it from the watch's monitoring FIT files into healthdata.db's events table, and the health-db worker carries the row over unchanged.

fact_time.description: events.fact_time: when the watch raised the alert, the FIT timestamp written by the ETL in UTC to the second. This is the fact time.

heart_rate.description: events.value: the heart rate that tripped the alert, in beats per minute. Garmin does not document the event; the ETL reads it from the high byte of FIT event 66's data field.

kind.description: events.kind: the ETL's name for the event. Only hr_high_alert rows become this type.

source_time.description: How the alert's time was read: value is the FIT timestamp, UTC by the format's definition (basis source).

value.description: The fact time as the source supplied it, as text and never rewritten: a date, a wall clock, an RFC 3339 string, or an epoch as its digits.

zone.description: The zone value is read in, and nothing else: an IANA name when one is known, UTC for a value that is UTC, else a fixed offset +HH:MM or -HH:MM. The gate refuses a name that is no zone.

basis.description: Who decided the zone. source: the source supplied it with the value, or the value is UTC by the source's own definition. configuration: a setting a person made for this source names it. assumption: the importer or writer chose it, with nothing behind it but its own default or the Definition's zone, and logged that it did.

source.description: events.source: the device family the ETL read, always "garmin" today.

threshold.description: events.threshold: the alert threshold configured on the watch, in beats per minute, from the low byte of the same FIT data field.

unit.description: events.unit: the unit of heart_rate and threshold, written by the ETL as "bpm".
